title_en: China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. v. China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Qingdao Office, Wang Zhigang, and Hu Jianjun — retrial of marine insurance contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: A person not a party to the case who has already assigned his creditor's right to another person and then, based on the assigned creditor's right, applies for retrial of the effective civil mediation agreement concerning that creditor's right has no legal basis and the application shall be dismissed. Where both parties to the contract, under circumstances where the losses can be substantially compensated, voluntarily reach a mediation agreement out of considerations such as litigation risk, such agreement should not be deemed as malicious collusion to abandon creditor's rights and harm the interests of a third party.
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over ship insurance contract; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Shandong Province; Shanghai Municipality; legal person; natural person; Insurance Law; Contract Law; standing of a person not a party to the case to apply for retrial; whether the mediation agreement constitutes malicious collusion; validity of ship insurance contract; dismissal of claims; ship insurance contract; machinery damage accident; assignment of claims; mediation agreement; good faith; contract dispute; insurance contract; application for retrial; Hu Jianjun ship insurance contract dispute
full_text_en:
China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. v. China Orient Asset Management Corporation Qingdao Office, Wang Zhigang, and Hu Jianjun — retrial of a dispute over a vessel insurance contract

[Ruling Summary]

Where a person not a party to the case has assigned its creditor's rights to another person and then applies for a retrial of an effective civil mediation document involving such rights based on the assigned rights, there is no legal basis for such application and it shall be dismissed. Where both parties to a contract voluntarily reach a mediation agreement out of considerations such as litigation risks under circumstances where the losses can be substantially compensated, it is not appropriate to find that they have maliciously colluded to waive creditor's rights to the detriment of a third party's interests.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 249

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Retrial Respondent): China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. Domicile: South Tower, Bank of Communications Financial Center, No. 190 Yin Cheng Zhong Lu, Pudong New District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Gao Guofu, Chairman of the Company.

Authorized Representative: Kou Feng, Staff Member of China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd.

Authorized Representative: Guo Yutao, Lawyer of Beijing Li Gefeng Law Firm.

Retrial Respondent (Person Not a Party at First and Second Instances, Original Retrial Applicant): China Orient Asset Management Corporation Qingdao Office. Domicile: 3rd Floor, Building B, No. 6 Gang Zhong Zhong Lu, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Responsible Person: Liu Bingwen, General Manager of the Office.

Retrial Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance, Original Retrial Respondent): Wang Zhigang, male, born on January 17, 1951, Han nationality, residing at Room 205, No. 55 Hebei Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Authorized Representative: Sun Jianming, male, born on November 24, 1971, Han nationality, residing at Room 301, Unit 2, Building 2, No. 7 Xing'an Zhi Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Retrial Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance, Original Retrial Respondent): Hu Jianjun, female, born in October 1957, Han nationality, residing at No. 55 Hebei Road, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

With respect to the dispute over a vessel insurance contract between the retrial applicant China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as CPIC Group) and the retrial respondents China Orient Asset Management Corporation Qingdao Office (hereinafter referred to as Orient Asset Qingdao Office), Wang Zhigang, and Hu Jianjun, the Shandong High People's Court rendered a civil judgment on September 6, 2010 (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62, which has become legally effective. Dissatisfied with that judgment, CPIC Group applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered a civil ruling on July 13, 2011 (2011) Min Zai Shen Zi No. 37, deciding to bring this case for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Wang Shumei, Judge Guo Zhonghong, and Acting Judge Yu Xiaohan, and held a public hearing on November 17, 2011. The authorized representatives of the retrial applicant CPIC Group, Guo Yutao and Kou Feng, and the authorized representative of the retrial respondent Wang Zhigang, Sun Jianming, appeared in court. The retrial respondents Orient Asset Qingdao Office and Hu Jianjun, after being lawfully summoned by this Court, did not appear in court. The case is now concluded.

The Qingdao Maritime Court found the following facts at first instance: Qingdao Rongguan Ship Leasing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qingdao Rongguan) purchased the vessel "Rong Sheng" from Fujian Provincial Grain Shipping Company on August 26, 1994. As Qingdao Rongguan did not have maritime transportation operation qualifications, it previously entered into a joint venture agreement with Hainan Antai Shipping Company on June 21, 1994, agreeing to register the vessel under the name of Hainan Antai Shipping Company for operation. Hainan Antai Shipping Company, as the owner of the vessel "Rong Sheng," registered the vessel with the Hainan Harbor Superintendence Administration on August 3, 1994, and obtained a certificate of vessel nationality. After obtaining the approval from the Ministry of Communications for external chartering, it bareboat chartered the vessel to Hong Kong Rongguan Shipping Company on September 7, 1994, for a term of one year, changed the vessel's flag to a flag of convenience, and obtained a certificate of registration issued by Saint Vincent and the Grenadines on October 19, 1994. On October 20, 1994, Qingdao Rongguan provided that certificate and vessel specifications to China Pacific Insurance Company Qingdao Branch (hereinafter referred to as Qingdao CPIC) for insurance, and Qingdao CPIC issued a vessel insurance policy on October 24. The policy stated: the insured was Qingdao Rongguan; the vessel name was "Rong Sheng"; the insured value and sum insured were both RMB 9,000,000; the insurance period was from 00:00 on November 1, 1994, to 00:00 on October 31, 1995; the deductible was RMB 70,000; the insurance conditions were all risks under the vessel insurance clauses of the People's Insurance Company of China (January 1, 1986). Subsequently, the vessel "Rong Sheng" was managed and operated by Qingdao Rongguan.

On March 5, 1995, the vessel "Rong Sheng" departed from Qingdao for Japan. On March 7, the vessel's port main engine malfunctioned and lost its operational capability. On March 23, the vessel returned from Japan using the starboard main engine and berthed at Beihai Shipyard dock on March 29. On April 22, Qingdao Huijie Maritime Safety Technical Consulting Service Company, at the request of Qingdao Rongguan, inspected the vessel and issued an inspection report indicating that the accident was caused by excessive clearance between the fourth cylinder main bearing shell replaced by the chief engineer and engineers during the repair of the port main engine and the crankshaft, resulting in insufficient lubrication. The report also recommended that the vessel proceed to Shanhaiguan Shipyard for permanent repair of the port main engine fault before April 30. From April 28 to July 17, 1995, the vessel "Rong Sheng" was repaired at Shanhaiguan Shipyard by Shanhaiguan Weihai Ship Mechanical and Electrical Co., Ltd. for the port main engine, and the costs incurred from the machinery damage amounted to RMB 2,460,978.11. After the main engine was repaired, the vessel "Rong Sheng" again departed from Qingdao for Shibushi Port, Japan on October 9, 1995. On October 11, while en route, the port main engine malfunctioned again. Using only the starboard main engine, the vessel arrived at Shibushi Port, Japan on October 18. After arrival, the crew lifted the cylinder head of the fourth cylinder of the main engine and found that the big end bearing shell was broken, the connecting rod and bearing were deformed, and the crankpin was cracked. Qingdao Rongguan promptly notified Qingdao CPIC and contacted Qingdao CPIC multiple times regarding the repair and inspection of the main engine. However, Qingdao CPIC did not respond until January 23, 1996, by fax to Qingdao Rongguan stating: "Regarding the repair quotation matters, please handle them yourself first, and we will decide after the liability is clarified." Subsequently, the vessel, arranged by Qingdao Rongguan, underwent necessary repairs at a Japanese port, departed on February 6, 1996, and arrived at the Qingdao port anchorage on February 15, 1996. On March 25, 1996, at the request of Qingdao Rongguan, a surveyor from the Qingdao Branch of the China Classification Society boarded the vessel at the Qingdao anchorage to inspect the cause, scope, and extent of the damage to the port main engine and issued an inspection report on April 18, indicating that the main engine damage was caused by the engineer's reduction of the oil pressure, which reduced the amount of oil entering the bearing, leading to deteriorating lubrication conditions. Qingdao Rongguan inquired about the replacement and repair of the port main engine crankshaft from relevant domestic and foreign manufacturers and found that the cost of spare parts alone was approximately RMB 4,000,000, and with inspection, service, and other costs, it could reach RMB 6,000,000 to 7,000,000. Before the vessel returned to Qingdao, Qingdao Rongguan had necessary repairs carried out at the Japanese port for the main engine fault, resulting in inspection, parts, and repair costs of approximately RMB 4,000,000. Given that the repair costs for the vessel would exceed the insured value of RMB 9,000,000, Qingdao Rongguan issued a notice of abandonment to Qingdao CPIC on April 21, 1996, which Qingdao CPIC received the next day but did not clearly indicate whether it accepted the abandonment. Regarding the two machinery damage incidents on the "Rong Sheng," Qingdao CPIC had previously paid RMB 800,000 to Qingdao Rongguan and advanced USD 100,000, totaling RMB 1,630,000.

On December 13, 1995, Qingdao Rongguan filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Maritime Court on the grounds that the vessel "Rong Sheng" had suffered two machinery damage incidents during the insurance period and had become a constructive total loss, requesting Qingdao CPIC to pay repair costs of RMB 3,115,238.64 and the constructive total loss of RMB 9,000,000, and to bear the litigation costs.

On July 16, 1996, Qingdao CPIC filed a counterclaim with the Qingdao Maritime Court, alleging that: Qingdao Rongguan was not the owner of the vessel "Rong Sheng" and had no insurable interest in the vessel; Qingdao Rongguan failed to truthfully disclose the fact that the vessel was bareboat chartered, and the insurance contract should automatically terminate. Qingdao CPIC requested Qingdao Rongguan to return the prepaid amount of RMB 800,000 and interest, repay the loan of USD 100,000, and bear the litigation costs.

The Qingdao Maritime Court held at first instance that: Qingdao Rongguan had fulfilled its duty of truthful disclosure at the time of insurance, and there was no fact that Qingdao Rongguan had bareboat chartered the vessel after the issuance of the insurance policy. Qingdao CPIC's claim that the insurance contract had automatically terminated could not be established. Qingdao Rongguan was responsible for the management and operation of the vessel "Rong Sheng" and bore all risks and liabilities, thus having an insurable interest in the vessel. The vessel insurance contract relationship between the parties was lawfully established and binding on both parties. The two machinery damage incidents on the "Rong Sheng" during the insurance period were both caused by the negligence of the engineers, falling within the scope of insurance coverage. Qingdao CPIC should bear compensation liability for the losses and reasonable expenses incurred thereby. Qingdao Rongguan should not return the compensation and advances already paid by Qingdao CPIC. After the second machinery damage incident on the "Rong Sheng," the total of temporary repair costs and permanent repair costs exceeded the insured value. Qingdao Rongguan had issued a notice of abandonment to Qingdao CPIC, which should be deemed as a constructive total loss, and Qingdao CPIC should pay compensation according to the sum insured of RMB 9,000,000. Qingdao CPIC's compensation amount included costs of RMB 2,460,978.11 arising from the first insurance incident and the payable amount of RMB 9,000,000 from the second insurance incident, deducting the already paid RMB 1,630,000 and the deductible of RMB 70,000, totaling RMB 9,760,978.11. Qingdao CPIC should also compensate for the interest loss on this amount, with interest calculated from the date Qingdao Rongguan issued the notice of abandonment. In summary, in accordance with Article 106, paragraph 1, and Article 111 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 237, 238, and 239 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered a civil judgment on June 25, 1998 (1996) Qing Hai Fa Hai Shang Chu Zi No. 15: 1. Qingdao CPIC shall pay insurance compensation of RMB 9,760,978.11 and bank deposit interest for the same period from April 22, 1996, to the date of effectiveness of this judgment to Qingdao Rongguan; 2. The counterclaim of Qingdao CPIC was dismissed.

Dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, Qingdao CPIC appealed to the Shandong High People's Court.

After the second-instance trial, the Shandong High People's Court found that the facts found by the Qingdao Maritime Court were substantially true. It also found: On October 11, 1995, after the port main engine of the "Rong Sheng" malfunctioned, the vessel arrived at Shibushi Port, Japan on October 18. On October 30, Han Zhenyuan, the chief engineer of Qingdao Ocean Shipping Company, boarded the "Rong Sheng" at Shibushi Port to be responsible for the repair of the vessel, and before November 14, repairs were completed for the damage to the fourth, fifth, and eighth cylinders of the port main engine. On November 14, surveyor Qian Dexing from the Osaka Office of the China Classification Society boarded the "Rong Sheng" for inspection. The surveyor inspected the damage and repair status of the fourth, fifth, and eighth cylinders of the port main engine but did not start the engine for testing, and left the vessel that same day. On November 28, 1995, the Osaka Office of the China Classification Society issued vessel survey report No. DB950108 based on the inspection on November 14, stating that the port main engine damage inspection and repair inspection of the "Rong Sheng" maintained class. However, the engine logbook of the "Rong Sheng" for November 16, 1995, recorded: "Port main engine No. 6 cylinder dismantled for inspection, bearing journal ground smooth." Subsequently, the vessel's crew organized repairs on the sixth cylinder. According to the testimony of surveyor Qian Dexing, in December 1995, the "Rong Sheng" side called to inform that when preparing to start the engine to return to China, it was discovered that the sixth cylinder crankpin was also damaged. Due to scheduling difficulties for the personnel of the Osaka Office of the China Classification Society, they could not immediately send someone to board the vessel for inspection, and later heard from the vessel side that the sixth cylinder had been repaired.

The Shandong High People's Court held at second instance that: The Qingdao Maritime Court's finding that Qingdao Rongguan had an insurable interest in the vessel "Rong Sheng" and that Qingdao Rongguan had fulfilled its duty of truthful disclosure at the time of insurance was consistent with the facts. Under the circumstances where the "Rong Sheng" was deemed a constructive total loss, Qingdao Rongguan issued a notice of abandonment to Qingdao CPIC, but Qingdao CPIC did not indicate acceptance of abandonment within a reasonable period, which should be deemed as refusal to accept abandonment. Qingdao CPIC's claim that the residual value of the "Rong Sheng" should be appraised and deducted from the insurance compensation lacked legal basis. The first-instance judgment found clear facts and applied the law appropriately. In accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered a civil judgment on July 12, 1999 (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533: Dismissed the appeal and affirmed the first-instance judgment.

Dissatisfied with the above second-instance judgment, Qingdao CPIC applied to the Shandong High People's Court for retrial on July 28, 1999, on the grounds that Qingdao Rongguan was suspected of insurance fraud. The court ruled to retry the case on November 14, 1999. During the retrial, with the mediation of the court, Qingdao Rongguan and Qingdao CPIC reached a mediation agreement: Qingdao Rongguan, due to incorrect disclosure regarding the first machinery damage incident of the "Rong Sheng," waived its claim for that incident; for the second machinery damage incident, Qingdao CPIC deducted the previously paid RMB 2,300,000 and paid an additional RMB 300,000 to Qingdao Rongguan, settling the case with a total compensation of RMB 2,600,000. The court issued a civil mediation document on March 30, 2000 (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190, confirming the above mediation agreement.

After the Shandong High People's Court issued the civil mediation document (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190, Orient Asset Qingdao Office, as a third party not involved in the case, filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court on January 8, 2002, on the grounds that Qingdao CPIC and Qingdao Rongguan had maliciously colluded to waive creditor's rights, preventing the realization of its due creditor's rights, requesting the revocation of the civil mediation document. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil ruling on March 3, 2003 (2002) Qing Zhi Chu Zi No. 10, dismissing the lawsuit filed by Orient Asset Qingdao Office on the grounds that dissatisfaction with the mediation document should be raised by way of appeal and not by filing a lawsuit. Dissatisfied with the ruling, Orient Asset Qingdao Office appealed to the Shandong High People's Court, which, after trial, rendered a civil ruling on October 13, 2003 (2003) Lu Min Er Zhong Zi No. 322: Dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original ruling. On November 25, 2005, Orient Asset Qingdao Office applied to this Court for retrial, requesting the revocation of the above civil mediation document. This Court sent a letter to the Shandong High People's Court for review. After review, the Shandong High People's Court rendered a civil ruling on January 25, 2010 (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62, deciding to retry the case. As Qingdao CPIC and Qingdao Rongguan had been dissolved, in that retrial, the Shandong High People's Court listed CPIC Group and the shareholders of Qingdao Rongguan, Wang Zhigang and Hu Jianjun, as retrial respondents.

In that retrial, the Shandong High People's Court further found: On August 16 and December 2, 1994, Qingdao Rongguan borrowed USD 550,000 in two installments from the Bank of China Qingdao High-Tech Industrial Park Sub-branch, and failed to repay upon maturity. The Bank of China Qingdao High-Tech Industrial Park Sub-branch filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court. After trial by the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court and the Shandong High People's Court, civil judgments were rendered (1998) Qing Jing Chu Zi No. 155 and (1999) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 52, ordering Qingdao Rongguan to repay the principal and interest (up to September 21, 1998) of USD 699,524.16 to the Bank of China Qingdao High-Tech Industrial Park Sub-branch. On July 26, 2000, the Bank of China Qingdao High-Tech Industrial Park Sub-branch assigned its creditor's rights against Qingdao Rongguan to Orient Asset Qingdao Office. Qingdao Rongguan had been dissolved on July 7, 2000, after being approved by the Qingdao Administration for Industry and Commerce. The enterprise registration records of Qingdao Rongguan showed that its shareholders were Wang Zhigang and Hu Jianjun. The shareholders' resolution signed by the two and the application for company dissolution registration signed by Wang Zhigang stated that Qingdao Rongguan had no creditor's rights or debts, but no liquidation was conducted. Qingdao CPIC was a branch without legal personality registered and established by CPIC Group (formerly known as China Pacific Insurance Company) on November 9, 1992, with the Shinan Branch of the Qingdao Administration for Industry and Commerce. CPIC Group applied to dissolve Qingdao CPIC in March 2006. After the Shandong High People's Court rendered the civil judgment (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533 in the dispute over the vessel insurance contract between Qingdao Rongguan and Qingdao CPIC, Qingdao CPIC had requested the court to stay enforcement. In its "Urgent Request Report on Staying Enforcement of the Shandong High People's Court (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533 Judgment" dated July 20, 1999, Qingdao CPIC stated: "The creditor's rights registered with the Qingdao Maritime Court by Qingdao Rongguan have reached over RMB 20,000,000."

The Shandong High People's Court held in retrial that: Qingdao CPIC was aware of Qingdao Rongguan's external debts, and the two parties reached a mediation agreement whereby Qingdao Rongguan waived its matured creditor's rights, resulting in the inability to realize the rights and interests of Orient Asset Qingdao Office. The mediation agreement should be revoked in accordance with the law. In accordance with Article 58, paragraph (4) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 52, paragraph (2) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 177 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered a civil judgment on September 6, 2010 (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62: Revoked the court's civil mediation document (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190.

Pacific Insurance Group, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62 of the Shandong High People's Court, filed an application for retrial with this Court, alleging: 1. The Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation had already transferred the creditor's rights involved in the case to Qingdao Tongdaxin Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qingdao Tongdaxin Company), and therefore had no right to apply for retrial against the Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190 of the Shandong High People's Court. 2. The Shandong High People's Court's finding that Qingdao Pacific Insurance and Qingdao Rongguan Company maliciously colluded to harm the interests of third parties lacked evidence and applied the law incorrectly. At the time of the mediation concluding the case between Qingdao Pacific Insurance and Qingdao Rongguan, Qingdao Pacific Insurance was unaware of the creditor's rights of the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation. Outside of the litigation, Qingdao Pacific Insurance separately paid Qingdao Rongguan insurance compensation of RMB 6.1 million yuan through mediation by the public security organs. The total insurance compensation paid by Qingdao Pacific Insurance to Qingdao Rongguan was RMB 8,812,486 yuan, plus the actual residual value of the ship obtained by Qingdao Rongguan of RMB 2.9 million yuan, making the actual total compensation paid by Qingdao Pacific Insurance RMB 11,712,486 yuan, which exceeded Qingdao Rongguan's total loss of RMB 11,460,978.11 yuan by RMB 251,508 yuan. Qingdao Rongguan did not actually waive its creditor's rights, nor did it harm the interests of other creditors. The failure of the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation to execute and recover this insurance compensation was due to its own failure to fully exercise its creditor's rights, and was unrelated to Qingdao Pacific Insurance. In the case (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62, the Shandong High People's Court should have conducted a full trial of the insurance contract dispute between Qingdao Pacific Insurance and Qingdao Rongguan under the second-instance procedure, but in fact only tried the claim of the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation to set aside the mediation letter, ignoring the insurance contract dispute and failing to make a substantive ruling on whether Qingdao Pacific Insurance should bear liability for compensation and how to bear such liability, seriously harming the interests of all parties. 3. The Civil Judgment (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533 of the Shandong High People's Court also contained obvious errors. While that second-instance judgment found that the "Rongsheng" vessel constituted a constructive total loss and ordered Qingdao Pacific Insurance to pay full compensation according to the insured amount, it ignored the right of Qingdao Pacific Insurance to the residual value of the insured subject matter, with the result that Qingdao Pacific Insurance could not obtain the proceeds of RMB 2.9 million yuan from the auction of the "Rongsheng" vessel by Qingdao Rongguan. 4. In the process of hearing the case (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62, the Shandong High People's Court named Pacific Insurance Group as the respondent, which was clearly improper. The rights and obligations under the property insurance involved in this case have been succeeded by the Qingdao Branch of China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd., and the respondent should be that branch. In summary, it requested the revocation of the Civil Judgment (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62 of the Shandong High People's Court and a judgment according to law maintaining the Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190 of that court.

Wang Zhigang responded: 1. The Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation had already transferred the creditor's rights to Qingdao Tongdaxin Company and had no right to assert claims in this case. 2. Before the "Rongsheng" vessel was auctioned, Qingdao Pacific Insurance refused to accept the abandonment of the vessel by Qingdao Rongguan, and the residual value of the vessel was unrelated to Qingdao Pacific Insurance. 3. The mediation agreement between Qingdao Pacific Insurance and Qingdao Rongguan was legally valid, and Qingdao Pacific Insurance had further compensated Qingdao Rongguan RMB 6.1 million yuan after the court mediation. It requested that the validity of the Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190 of the Shandong High People's Court be maintained.

The Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation did not appear at the retrial hearing of this Court and did not submit a written reply, but during the review of the retrial application by this Court, it submitted a written opinion stating: 1. Qingdao Pacific Insurance knew that Qingdao Rongguan owed debts of over RMB 20 million yuan to third parties, and negotiating with Qingdao Rongguan to waive creditor's rights would cause its corresponding debts to be unsatisfied, harming the interests of other creditors. 2. Before the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation acquired the creditor's rights in this case, the original creditor, the Bank of China Qingdao High-tech Industrial Park Sub-branch, had already applied for enforcement against Qingdao Rongguan, which was consolidated with the enforcement case of Qingdao Rongguan applying for enforcement against Qingdao Pacific Insurance. It was precisely due to the malicious collusion between Qingdao Pacific Insurance and Qingdao Rongguan that the enforcement was suspended, harming the interests of the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation. 3. The claim by Pacific Insurance Group that Qingdao Pacific Insurance paid insurance compensation of RMB 6.1 million yuan was false. According to the Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190 of the Shandong High People's Court, the amount paid by Qingdao Pacific Insurance through mediation was only RMB 300,000 yuan, not over RMB 8 million yuan. 4. Qingdao Pacific Insurance, as an unincorporated institution, was established and subsequently dissolved by Pacific Insurance Group, and Pacific Insurance Group should succeed to the rights and obligations of its branch. In summary, the Civil Judgment (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62 of the Shandong High People's Court found clear facts and correctly applied the law. It requested the rejection of Pacific Insurance Group's retrial application.

Hu Jianjun did not submit a reply.

This Court finds: The facts already found by the Qingdao Maritime Court and the Shandong High People's Court are supported by relevant evidence, and no party raised any objection; this Court confirms them.

During the retrial of this Court, Pacific Insurance Group provided evidence including eight vouchers for compensation paid by Qingdao Pacific Insurance to Qingdao Rongguan, legal documents such as the transaction confirmation for the sale of the "Rongsheng" vessel by the Qingdao Maritime Court, enforcement rulings (1999) Qing Zhi Zi No. 211 and (2010) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 125 of the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court, and the business registration materials of Qingdao Tongdaxin Company. The above evidence consists of original documents or copies verified against the original documents, respectively proving important facts such as the compensation paid by Qingdao Pacific Insurance, the residual value of the "Rongsheng" vessel, and the transfer of the creditor's rights in the case. One compensation receipt indicates that Wang Zhigang, on behalf of Qingdao Rongguan, signed and received the ship insurance compensation of RMB 6.1 million yuan paid by Qingdao Pacific Insurance on March 31, 2000. Wang Zhigang also confirmed this fact in his reply, and this Court confirms it. The Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation claimed that the payment of RMB 6.1 million yuan was false, but did not provide sufficient countervailing evidence; this Court does not accept that claim. As for the other evidence mentioned above, the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation, Wang Zhigang, and Hu Jianjun did not raise any objections, and this Court confirms its probative value.

Based on the above evidence, this Court further finds: From September 15, 1995, to February 2, 1996, Qingdao Pacific Insurance paid a total of RMB 1.94 million yuan in advance insurance compensation to Qingdao Rongguan. During the trial of the case of Qingdao Ocean Foreign Labor Service Cooperation Co., Ltd. v. Hainan Antai Shipping Company and Qingdao Rongguan concerning a crew labor contract dispute [case (1996) Qing Hai Fa Hai Shang Chu Zi No. 142], upon the application of Qingdao Ocean Foreign Labor Service Cooperation Co., Ltd., the Qingdao Maritime Court on January 9, 1997, after failing to auction the "Rongguan" vessel then owned by Hainan Antai Shipping Company and Qingdao Rongguan, sold the vessel on site for RMB 2.909 million yuan. After trial by the Shandong High People's Court, a final judgment was rendered on November 19, 1998: 1. Qingdao Rongguan shall pay Qingdao Ocean Foreign Labor Service Cooperation Co., Ltd. labor remuneration of USD 306,607.28 and RMB 88,390 yuan plus interest; 2. This maritime claim has a maritime lien. After the Shandong High People's Court issued the Civil Judgment (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533 on July 12, 1999, the Qingdao Maritime Court, in enforcing the creditor's rights of Qingdao Ocean Foreign Labor Service Cooperation Co., Ltd. and other creditors against Qingdao Rongguan, on July 28, 1999, and August 5, 1999, respectively, deducted and transferred from Qingdao Pacific Insurance RMB 1,182,728 yuan and RMB 57,758 yuan. After the Shandong High People's Court issued the Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190 on March 30, 2000, the Qingdao Maritime Court on June 2, 2000, and November 23, 2001, respectively, returned enforcement funds of RMB 200,000 yuan and RMB 300,000 yuan to Qingdao Pacific Insurance. Thus, the Qingdao Maritime Court actually compulsorily deducted a total of RMB 740,486 yuan from Qingdao Pacific Insurance. On March 31, 2000, Qingdao Pacific Insurance paid RMB 6.1 million yuan in ship insurance compensation to Qingdao Rongguan.

During the enforcement of the final judgment in the loan contract dispute case between Bank of China Qingdao High-tech Industrial Park Sub-branch and Qingdao Rongguan [Civil Judgment (1998) Qing Jing Chu Zi No. 155 of that court], the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court, upon examination, found that Bank of China Qingdao High-tech Industrial Park Sub-branch transferred the creditor's rights in that case to the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation on July 26, 2000, and the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation further transferred those creditor's rights to Qingdao Tongdaxin Company on October 15, 2004. Accordingly, on August 31, 2010, that court issued the Enforcement Ruling (2010) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 125, changing the enforcement applicant in that case to Qingdao Tongdaxin Company.

This Court holds that this case is a dispute over a ship insurance contract. Considering the allegations and defenses of Pacific Insurance Group, the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation, and Wang Zhigang, the focus of the dispute in this case is whether the Shandong High People's Court had sufficient factual and legal basis to set aside its Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190 by its Civil Judgment (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62.

Before filing the retrial application against the Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190 of the Shandong High People's Court, the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation had, on October 15, 2004, transferred the creditor's rights involved in the case to Qingdao Tongdaxin Company, and thus had no interest in this case. The application for retrial by the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation, based on its already transferred creditor's rights, has no factual or legal basis.

Pacific Insurance Group, as the legal person enterprise that established and subsequently dissolved its branch Qingdao Pacific Insurance, should bear the liability for clearing the debts left by Qingdao Pacific Insurance after its dissolution. The Shandong High People's Court, in the process of hearing the case (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62, listed Pacific Insurance Group as the respondent, which was not improper.

After the Shandong High People's Court issued the Civil Judgment (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533 on July 12, 1999, for the creditor's rights of Qingdao Rongguan recognized in that judgment of RMB 9,760,978.11 yuan and its interest, the Qingdao Maritime Court, in enforcing that judgment, actually compulsorily deducted from Qingdao Pacific Insurance a total of RMB 740,486 yuan from July 28, 1999, to November 23, 2001; Qingdao Pacific Insurance separately paid ship insurance compensation of RMB 6.1 million yuan to Qingdao Rongguan on March 31, 2000, outside the procedural framework of this case. These two items of compensation total RMB 6,840,486 yuan, which is RMB 2,920,492.11 yuan less than the principal of the creditor's rights confirmed in the above judgment. After the "Rongsheng" vessel suffered a second engine damage incident constituting a constructive total loss, Qingdao Rongguan sent a notice of abandonment to Qingdao Pacific Insurance on April 21, 1996, but Qingdao Pacific Insurance did not notify Qingdao Rongguan of its decision to accept or not accept the abandonment within a reasonable time as required by Article 249, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code of the PRC. It should be determined that Qingdao Pacific Insurance did not accept the abandonment, and Qingdao Pacific Insurance should not acquire rights to the residual value of the "Rongsheng" vessel. In the Civil Judgment (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533, the Shandong High People's Court confirmed that Qingdao Pacific Insurance should pay full compensation according to the insured amount without deducting the residual value of the vessel; this had sufficient factual and legal basis. Although Qingdao Pacific Insurance was not entitled to claim the residual value of the "Rongsheng" vessel, considering the fact that Qingdao Rongguan actually obtained the ship's residual value of RMB 2.909 million yuan, Qingdao Rongguan's losses have been substantially compensated.

On the ground that Qingdao Rongguan was suspected of insurance fraud, Qingdao Pacific Insurance applied for retrial against the Civil Judgment (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533 of the Shandong High People's Court. During the retrial of that judgment, the Shandong High People's Court presided over the voluntary mediation between Qingdao Pacific Insurance and Qingdao Rongguan and, on March 30, 2000, issued the Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190, confirming the mediation agreement between the two parties. When it was unclear whether the retrial application filed by Qingdao Pacific Insurance against the Civil Judgment (1998) Lu Jing Zhong Zi No. 533 of the Shandong High People's Court would be sustained, and given that Qingdao Rongguan's losses could be largely compensated, it was not improper for Qingdao Pacific Insurance and Qingdao Rongguan, each considering factors such as litigation risks, to voluntarily reach a mediation agreement. During the retrial of its Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190, the Shandong High People's Court failed to ascertain the basic facts that the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation had already transferred the creditor's rights to Qingdao Tongdaxin Company and that Qingdao Pacific Insurance had separately paid Qingdao Rongguan RMB 6.1 million yuan in compensation. It still treated the Qingdao Office of Orient Asset Management Corporation as the creditor in the case and found that Qingdao Pacific Insurance and Qingdao Rongguan had maliciously colluded to waive creditor's rights, harming the interests of third parties, and thereby set aside the above civil mediation letter. This had no factual or legal basis. Pacific Insurance Group's request to set aside the Civil Judgment (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62 of the Shandong High People's Court is well-founded, and this Court supports it.

In summary, the Civil Judgment (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62 of the Shandong High People's Court found unclear facts and incorrectly applied the law, and should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 130 and Article 153, paragraph 1, items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment by default is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2007) Lu Min Jian Zi No. 62 of the Shandong High People's Court;

2. Maintain the Civil Mediation Letter (1999) Lu Jing Jian Zi No. 190 of the Shandong High People's Court.

This judgment is final.
